title: Select and move part of a picture, resize the canvas, one Shape tool.
notes: Select area, a new tool (G): drag over part of the picture, then drag it somewhere else. It lifts off as a picture you can move, resize, turn or delete; hold ⌥ / Alt to drag a copy. ⌘X cuts the area, ⌘C copies it, ⌫ deletes it.
Change the canvas size by dragging the handles on the image's edge: outward to add space around the picture, inward to trim it.
Rectangle and Ellipse are one tool now, Shape: pick which in the side panel, where a selected shape can also be turned into the other. R and E still pick them.
New starts at the size of the image on the clipboard, when there is one, so it can be pasted onto a canvas that fits it.
A pasted image keeps its own size whenever the canvas can hold it; it used to shrink to 80% of the canvas.
Marks reaching past the canvas edge are cut off there on screen, as they are in the saved image.
A copied mark also goes on the clipboard as a picture, so it can be pasted into a new image (which opens at its size) or another app.
⌘X / Ctrl+X also cuts a selected mark.
